title: Break and recover four M2.5 HELICOIL tangs from an ODRI actuator shell base
objective: Finish four already-installed M2.5 × 3.75 mm HELICOIL inserts in a representative ODRI actuator shell base: align and hold the specified straight tang break-off mandrel in each insert, strike it with a separately manipulated hammer to fracture the tang at its manufactured notch, then physically recover every released tang into a tray without damaging the retained inserts or shell.
skills: precision grasping of a narrow mandrel
coaxial alignment with recessed M2.5 inserts
success_conditions: Full success requires four contact-loaded fractures at the modeled notches, four independently simulated free tangs physically deposited in a containment tray, no tang remaining in or escaping from the shell, every insert retained within frozen pose tolerances, no shell or coil damage, all tools released, and a two-second stable final state. Partial credit may cover safe alignment or fewer completed fractures only while every released fragment remains contained. Insufficient or repeated impacts, glancing blows, off-axis overload, insert displacement, shell damage, tool jamming, fragment loss, or any pose/velocity injection invalidates full success.
industrial_value: The pinned ODRI robot-actuator procedure requires four M2.5 × 3.75 mm inserts in the shell base, removal of their tangs, and verification that tangs do not remain inside the part. Böllhoff documents notch fracture and identifies the M2.5 straight tang break-off mandrel.
dexterity: One arm must maintain a narrow mandrel coaxially inside a small recessed insert while the other delivers a controlled hammer impact. The robot must avoid lateral loading of the retained coil and printed boss, withdraw the mandrel without snagging, and recover four small loose metal fragments from an open shell cavity.

asset_plan: Build an independently authored representative rigid fixture rather than claiming an exact current-product replica. The four inspected pinned ODRI images establish four marked shell-base insert bosses, vertical installation access, the open cavity and large through-openings, and completed inserts. Use the documented M2.5 × 3.75 mm insert and Böllhoff M2.5 mandrel family to anchor the local interaction. Treat the historical unitless STL and 2019 v1 overview only as explicitly outdated geometry references. Model retained coil proxies, separate tangs, manufactured notches, mandrel, hammer, shell, and tray as native rigid PhysX bodies. Freeze and disclose uncited wire, notch, handle, friction, fracture-load, impulse, damage, and tolerance values as prototype assumptions. Before YAM integration, validate contact-driven axial fracture, insufficient and repeated impacts, glancing blows, off-axis damage, coil retention, freely moving fragment containment, reset freshness, callback timing, force/impulse/energy logging, timestep convergence, and failure controls in the pinned runtime.
risk: Exact notch strength and tool-handle dimensions are not published and must remain frozen testable assumptions. The inspected images support a representative accessible cavity fixture but not exact CAD correspondence to the outdated STL. Native PhysX may fail to provide stable millimetre-scale impact fracture or fragment behavior; that is a later component-test rejection condition. Early comparison found different central outcomes from automatic center punching (one dent), nail hammering (fastener penetration), blind riveting (joining plus spent-stem disposal), PCB/tile depaneling (supported bulk fracture), and slide-hammer extraction (momentum-driven pin removal). Full fresh catalog, board, team, and six-suite novelty review remains mandatory after selection.
